origin.description: M1–M3 as in manifest.json; M3 is the closest-described moderation specification. Regulation regular-season decision plays, terminal two-minute exclusion, pre-play score difference minus one, split quadratic/linear performance with jump, continuous remaining minutes and all three performance-by-time products, full explicit controls, offense-team and season effects. Conditional likelihood and conventional covariance are inferred origins, not confirmed software settings. Missing conference membership and prediction conventions require resolution. Wider grid is OFF; no automatic Cartesian execution or target-based choice.

levels.description: Exclude plays at or below 120 seconds remaining in regulation.
Exclude only plays strictly below 120 seconds, retaining a decision stamped exactly 02:00.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: D01 PDF pp. 15–16, Endnote 3 invokes the last two minutes and the warning but does not specify boundary inclusion; this is a narrow unresolved sample difference.

levels.description: Retain actual executed decision plays; exclude administrative no-play events. Flag unusual actions for documented adjudication.
Include nullified fourth-down plays if their descriptions establish an actual attempted conversion, punt, or kick; still exclude timeouts and period markers.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 8 describes decisions rather than provider play-type codes. A nullified snap can embody a decision even if it is not an official statistical play; its inclusion is not specified. No arbitrary all-penalties exclusion is justified.

axes.notes: Cannot resolve from sample-size matching. Kneels, fakes and aborted kicks remain additional coding questions; no unsupported default labels are invented.

axes.decision: Measurement and orientation of deadline time

levels.description: Fractional minutes remaining from the pre-play seconds clock; uncentered.
Use quarters remaining as a single ordinal regressor, regenerating all time interactions.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 9 explicitly reports this robustness analysis, but coarsening time changes the design matrix and estimand. Exact ordinal convention is not supplied.

levels.description: Use elapsed minutes = 60 - minutes remaining, retaining and transforming all lower-order terms and interactions.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.rationale: The fixed-duration period in D01 PDF p. 9 makes this an affine reparameterization of the same complete model. Map coefficient signs and contrasts back to remaining time and preserve the same sample and controls.

source.where: Deadline Proximity; PDF p. 11, interaction terms

axes.decision: Affirmative versus complemented binary control coding

levels.description: Same-division, same-conference and home-field indicators coded affirmatively, with unknown codes flagged.
Complement a binary control and transform the intercept/team effects and its coefficient consistently, preserving the exact observations and semantic categories.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 9 defines binary control concepts but not codes. Complementation preserves the column space with an intercept or group intercepts; fitted probabilities and transformed contrasts agree. It does not authorize swapping division and conference labels or redefining membership.

axes.notes: The controls cannot be removed. Semantic ambiguity is not solved by this algebraic equivalence; model-based outputs must be mapped to the same coding.

levels.description: Conditional maximum likelihood with offensive franchise as panel and separate season indicators; inferred from xtlogit and team/year effects.
Unconditional logistic maximum likelihood with explicit offense-team and season indicators.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 9 describes fixed effects but does not give options. Unconditional and conditional likelihoods differ in nuisance-effect treatment and finite-sample estimation, so this plausible interpretation must not be called numerically equivalent. It also changes how probability predictions can be constructed.

axes.notes: No clustering axis is instantiated: the article does not supply a native cluster method or justify alternative cluster definitions. Record this as missing inference documentation, not an invitation to manufacture a grid.

axes.decision: Indicator inclusion in the controls-only model

levels.description: M1 follows Table 5 and omits below_indicator; M2 and M3 include it.
Include below_indicator in M1 as well as M2 and M3.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 9 says the indicator is included in each model, whereas Table 5 on p. 11 has blank M1 cells. This is an unresolved contradiction; it is not an equivalent change to the explicit table control list.

axes.notes: Applies only to M1 and its model-comparison test; all other controls fixed.

levels.description: A common complete-case sample for the union of M1–M3 variables; proposed, not reported.
Use complete cases separately for each model, recording all exclusions and estimating LR comparisons only on a common sample.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 11 reports model observations but never states a missingness protocol. The alternatives coincide only if the resulting cases coincide; that cannot be presumed without data.

axes.notes: No imputation or fabricated classifications. The reader does not access data to decide equivalence.

levels.description: At d=0, report the derivative approaching from below, with the below indicator equal to one; explicitly label the side.

source.where: Table 6 / zero column; PDF p. 9, jump indicator

levels.description: Report the right-hand derivative at the threshold, with the above-regime limit.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 9 permits a jump, and Table 6 on p. 12 reports an effect at zero without explaining its side. Left and right derivatives differ and the ordinary two-sided derivative may not exist. Neither choice can be selected by matching a printed result.

axes.notes: A finite one-point crossing effect is a distinct estimand, not a derivative substitute; it remains outside the equivalent set.

levels.description: Aspiration is the opposing pre-play score plus one point.
Replace aspiration with a benchmark based on recently held point spreads, once its exact lag/window and resetting rule are supplied.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4 reports an alternative-aspiration check. It changes the substantive performance reference and cannot be an equivalent specification. Currently incomplete and not executable.

axes.notes: Wider robustness family only; OFF pending documentary clarification. Do not invent a recent-spread statistic.

axes.decision: Choice-set and field-position restrictions in narrative robustness

levels.description: All eligible fourth-down decisions, conversion versus either punt or field goal.
Conversion versus kick within field-goal range, with documented range and third-choice treatment required.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4 reports this restricted outcome-choice model. It changes population and choice set and is a separate robustness estimand, not a substitute for the main outcome.

levels.description: Conversion versus punt outside field-goal range, with documented range and third-choice treatment required.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4 reports this separate restricted analysis. The cutoff is absent; it is not equivalent to the main sample or the inside-range analysis.

axes.notes: Wider robustness family only; OFF pending specification. Alternative levels are distinct models, never pooled as an interchangeable outcome grid.

fixed_not_varied: Primary population is the 2000–2005 regular-season regulation fourth-down decision set (D01 PDF p. 8, Data; PDF p. 15, Endnotes 1–2).
Primary outcome is the conversion decision, not its success or a win-probability model output (D01 PDF p. 8, Risk Taking).

M1–M3 retain total points, yards to first down, yards to touchdown, division, conference, home field, season week and deadline measure (D01 PDF p. 9, controls; PDF p. 11, Table 5). Explicit controls never vary within the equivalent set.
M2 and M3 retain both spline pieces, the below quadratic and jump indicator; M3 retains every stated time interaction and its main effects (D01 PDF pp. 9,11).
Team and season heterogeneity adjustment is retained; replacing it with game effects or a team-by-season interaction is not supported as an equivalent change (D01 PDF p. 9, Data Analysis Model).
Table 6 evaluation points are the stated gap grid and 53,38,23,8 minutes. These are analysis settings, not rounded estimates to retune (D01 PDF p. 12, Table 6 note).

excluded_alternatives.description: Drop explicit controls, choose a model by agreement, or invert/swap division and conference labels because the descriptive targets appear odd.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: No article basis; explicit controls in D01 PDF p. 9 and Table 5 p. 11 must remain. Publication anomalies cannot supply a coding rule.

excluded_alternatives.description: Use provider win probabilities, betting spreads or expected points as performance or aspiration.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: D01 PDF p. 9 defines a current-score aspiration. Available provider model columns and odds lines measure other constructs (data_description/data_dictionary.md).

excluded_alternatives.description: Treat the final two minutes, overtime or postseason as equivalent extensions of the primary sample.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: D01 PDF pp. 15–16, Endnotes 1–3 explicitly exclude them for theoretical reasons.

excluded_alternatives.description: Swap to probit, linear probability, random-effects logit, arbitrary clustering grids or alternative fixed-effect combinations.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: No such alternatives are supported in the supplied article; absence of detail is recorded as a question rather than a quota of unsupported specifications (D01 PDF p. 9, Data Analysis Model).

excluded_alternatives.description: Replace marginal effects at mean covariates with averaged individual marginal effects as an equivalent result.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: D01 PDF pp. 12–13, Figures 2–3 specify control means; nonlinear averaging changes the estimand. Exact Table 6 evaluation remains an open question.

excluded_alternatives.description: Infer alternative-aspiration windows or a field-goal threshold from general football knowledge.
excluded_alternatives.why_excluded: D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4 omits those definitions. The referenced robustness material is unavailable.
